checked_sources.source: Zhang, Xu & Chen 2012, The Exact Likelihood Ratio Test for Equality of Two Normal Populations
checked_sources.result: Confirms that the equal-distribution two-normal likelihood-ratio statistic has an exact finite-sample distribution. This was not imported as the power certificate below because r69 needs an alternative-side lower-tail guarantee plus SNML/burn-in penalties, but it is a promising tightening route.

derived_results.claim: The r68 conditional-SNML candidate admits a clean pathwise lower bound in terms of a two-sample Gaussian GLR minus four explicit MLE-overfit penalties and the exact SNML regrets.
derived_results.statement: Let the true pre/post laws be P=N(a,u), Q=N(c,v). Let each segment use burn-in b>=2, scored pre block A of length m=T-b and scored post block B of length n=H-b. Define G(A,B)=lhat(A)+lhat(B)-lhat(A union B), D_R(Z)=lhat(Z)-l_R(Z)>=0 and r_b(s)=sum_{j=b+1}^s d_j for the exact Gaussian SNML regret increments. The r68 exact identity and lhat(burn+score)>=l_R(burn+score) imply pathwise: log C >= G(A,B)-D_P(A)-D_Q(B)-D_P(burn_pre)-D_Q(burn_post)-r_b(T)-r_b(H). No asymptotics are used in this reduction.

derived_results.claim: For an exact candidate split, the pathwise reduction yields an explicit precommittable 1-beta lower confidence bound on log C using only Gaussian/chi-square quantiles, the true normalized change parameters and the exact SNML regret sequence.
derived_results.statement: Set epsilon=beta/12. For a Gaussian block of length q, Y_q=sample_MLE_variance/true_variance has q Y_q ~ chi-square(q-1). Let y_q^- and y_q^+ be the epsilon and 1-epsilon quantiles divided by q, and z=sqrt(chi-square_1^{-1}(1-epsilon)). Then the MLE-overfit term obeys D_R(block)<=K(q,epsilon):=(q/2) max_{y in {y_q^-,y_q^+}}[-log y+y-1]+z^2/2 on the joint variance/mean event. For the scored pre/post GLR, let lambda=m/(m+n), d_-=(|c-a|-z sqrt(u/m)-z sqrt(v/n))_+, Avar in [u y_m^-,u y_m^+], Bvar in [v y_n^-,v y_n^+]. A simultaneous lower bound is Gbar=(m+n)/2 times the minimum over that rectangle of log(lambda Avar+(1-lambda) Bvar+lambda(1-lambda)d_-^2)-lambda log Avar-(1-lambda)log Bvar. In log-variance coordinates this objective is convex (log-sum-exp minus a linear term), so the two-dimensional box minimization is globally solvable. Therefore with probability at least 1-beta, log C >= Gbar-K(m,epsilon)-K(n,epsilon)-2K(b,epsilon)-r_b(T)-r_b(H). A candidate of scale weight w_j and start mass pi_k is prospectively certified to cross the global PFA threshold whenever this lower bound is at least log[1/(alpha w_j pi_k)].

derived_results.claim: A weak-information scale should not spend changepoint prior mass before there is enough pre-change history to support its finite-sample certificate; precommitted delayed activation is PFA-valid and improves finite-threshold power without recycling capital.
derived_results.statement: Give each scale a fixed mass w_j and define its candidate start schedule only from a deterministic eligibility time T0_j onward. The first eligible candidate can use that scale's pi_1 because no earlier candidate at that scale ever received the mass. This is not renormalization after seeing data: it is a fixed support restriction of the prior. Later candidate masses remain the same summable sequence. The construction therefore stays within the r68 fixed-weight mixture proof while avoiding underpowered early starts and their needless log(1/pi_k) penalties.

derived_results.claim: A first conservative three-scale Gaussian PFA bank can cover canonical mean-only and variance-only alternatives at KL floors 1.0, 0.5 and 0.25 with 52 individualized split states plus three future-tail states, under an exact-split beta=0.10 power certificate.
derived_results.setup: Normalize P=N(0,1) by location/scale equivariance. Use alpha=0.05, beta=0.10, burn-in b=16, equal scale weights w_j=1/3 and the r68 telescoping log-heavy start prior. Canonical floor alternatives are mean-only Q=N(sqrt(2I),1), variance-up/down Q=N(0,r) where 0.5[-log r+r-1]=I. Start-index k is local to the precommitted scale activation.
derived_results.stress_check: For each canonical floor alternative, the certified margin was re-evaluated at several later candidate times through T=10000 using the growing pi_k penalty; in the sampled grid the smallest margin remained the activation-time variance-up margin and all later sampled margins increased because additional pre-change information outweighed the logarithmic start penalty. This is a numerical design check, not yet a theorem for every T or every Gaussian alternative with KL>=I_floor.
derived_results.scope: The 52-state count is ceil(384/16)+ceil(512/32)+ceil(768/64)=52, plus one collapsed future-tail state per scale. It does not yet include a formal penalty for split/changepoint misalignment up to g_j, so the spacing values are engineering choices pending r70.

derived_results.claim: The r69 prospective lower bound is conservative but behaved as a genuine lower certificate in the tested Monte Carlo paths.
derived_results.details: Using 300 fresh common-setup paths for each of six cases at the three design activation points and fixed H, the realized exact r68 log C was above the deterministic r69 lower bound in 300/300 paths for every case, and all 300/300 paths crossed the corresponding first-candidate threshold. Cases were I=1 mean and variance-up at T=256,H=384; I=0.5 mean and variance-up at T=500,H=512; I=0.25 mean and variance-up at T=1024,H=768. The realized 10th-percentile log C was far above the certificate (for example 48.55 vs 6.55 nats for I=1 variance-up and 56.29 vs 7.41 for I=0.25 variance-up), showing substantial room to tighten the power bound. Monte Carlo is an engineering check only; the 1-beta statement comes from the exact Gaussian quantile/union-bound construction.

candidates_new.mechanism: Select candidate lifetime before seeing post-change data by solving the explicit Gaussian lower-confidence certificate including SNML regret, MLE-overfit, PFA scale weight and changepoint prior penalty.
candidates_new.evidence: Pathwise reduction plus exact Gaussian/chi-square quantile events; no null Monte Carlo is used for validity.
candidates_new.scope: Exact candidate split and well-specified Gaussian pre/post laws; power probability 1-beta, separate from global PFA alpha.
candidates_new.confidence: high for the stated scoped certificate; conservative in finite samples.

candidates_new.mechanism: Delay each information-floor scale until a deterministic minimum prefix length, start that scale's fixed prior only then, and use larger spacing/lifetime for weaker floors so total individualized state stays bounded in the first design.
candidates_new.evidence: Fixed-support prior validity plus the r69 certificate and normalized Gaussian design solve.
candidates_new.scope: First three-scale design is certified only for canonical exact-split floor alternatives and numerically spot-checked over later candidate times; split mismatch and the full KL-floor alternative manifold remain open.
candidates_new.confidence: medium-high as a design mechanism, medium for the current numeric grid.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Use independent lower/upper bounds in the pooled-variance numerator and segment-variance denominators to lower-bound the Gaussian GLR.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected as too loose. That naive decoupling can make the bound strongly negative even at moderate KL. Preserving the shared variance variables and minimizing the exact GLR expression jointly in log-variance coordinates restores a useful finite-sample certificate.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: A KL floor alone immediately yields a universal fixed H for every Gaussian alternative and every candidate time.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Not established. r69 solved canonical mean-only and variance-only floor representatives and spot-checked later times. A proof over the entire mean/variance KL level set and explicit split-misalignment contamination is still required before claiming universal coverage.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: The r69 certificate is close to the empirical lower tail and therefore near-optimal.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected by engineering evidence. Realized 10th-percentile log evidence exceeded the bound by tens of nats in the tested cases, so exact two-normal LRT distributional tools or sharper joint concentration may substantially shrink H/state without changing PFA validity.

frontier: Prove the r69 canonical design over the entire normalized Gaussian KL level set {Q: D_KL(Q||P)>=I_floor}, or find the true worst direction; do not assume mean-only/variance-only endpoints are worst without proof.

Add split/changepoint misalignment to the prospective certificate. Bound the loss when the nearest candidate start is up to g_j observations early or late, then optimize g_j rather than treating spacing as an engineering constant.

Tighten the beta-power certificate using the exact finite-sample two-normal likelihood-ratio distribution or a joint concentration inequality so the large observed gap between the deterministic bound and empirical lower tail can be converted into smaller H/state.

Turn the sampled later-time margin observation into a theorem: show when increasing prefix T dominates the log(1/pi_k) growth so fixed H_j remains sufficient after deterministic scale activation, or derive the minimal safe H_j(k) growth law.
Construct an evidence/capacity stopping-time kill rule that uses the r68 safe-kill theorem and prove its additional detection-delay loss relative to the deterministic H_j bank.

Benchmark the separable sum-of-infs detector against the exact Saha-Ramdas shared-null infimum-after-sum detector under matched PFA and common-random Gaussian changes, measuring the price of separability directly.
Extend beyond Gaussian only by replacing the exact quantile certificate with an explicitly valid robust null/alternative class; current PFA and power claims must not be generalized to heavy tails.
exact_next_action: Parameterize the normalized Gaussian KL level set by variance ratio r and mean shift squared Delta^2=2I+log r-r+1, minimize the r69 prospective lower bound over all feasible r for each of the three scales, and identify the true worst change direction. Then incorporate an early/late split offset d in [0,g_j] as a two-component contaminated segment and re-solve {T0_j,g_j,H_j,w_j} under the same 52-state target. If the joint bound remains excessively conservative, use the exact two-normal LRT distribution as the next tightening route while keeping the global e-process PFA proof unchanged.
